top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock is a single, well-defined invention (magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms) with independent reproduction at the 10^-18 level and a two-name allocation, Katori and Ye, that leaves no forced omission among the supplied names. It is distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-quantum-system prizes because its limits are set by many-body physics. P001 is a strong second: a real new organising principle, but with the visible Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang gap in credit, which I rank above no award.
recusal_note: Possible connection: my documented research stay in John Hall's laboratory; Hall is not a credited name in P002, so no recusal ground is apparent, but I note it. No other connection to Katori, Ye, Kane, Mele or Molenkamp apparent from profile.
